decisions.decision: Bracket the two lazy-init private helpers (__GetOrCreateChartMarkers, __GetOrCreateDiscourse) inside the helper, not at the call site
decisions.why: Both are invoked before their Create method enters its own _TransactionCM, so a call-site bracket would leave DiscourseDataOA/ChartMarkersOA creation unbracketed; _TransactionCM is nesting-aware so a future caller can still wrap them
decisions.rejected: Bracketing at the Create call sites, or hoisting the helper call inside Create-s existing with-block

decisions.decision: Keep hasattr capability checks and membership tests outside the transaction in AddDependentClause and the two lazy-init guards
decisions.why: A redundant add or an already-initialised slot stays a true no-op instead of opening an empty named undo entry that Phase 2 would also Rollback(0)
decisions.rejected: Wrapping the whole conditional including the guard

decisions.decision: For reference setters shaped `if x is None: obj.XRA = None else: x = resolve(...); obj.XRA = x`, hoist the resolution out of both branches so it runs before the transaction opens, leaving a single assignment inside one bracket
decisions.why: Resolution can raise; hoisting it means an unresolvable reference raises without opening an empty named undo entry that Phase 2 would Rollback(0). Also collapses two bracket sites into one per method. Applied to the five WfiMorphBundle setters in batch 8; the same shape recurs in Notebook/Grammar/Lexicon
decisions.rejected: Bracketing each assignment separately in its own branch, which opens a transaction after the raising resolve call

decisions.decision: D6 - a mutation deliberately hoisted OUT of a transaction still needs a transaction of its own. AnthropologyOperations.Create keeps its AnthroListOA hoist but gets a separate named bracket ('Create anthropology list'); the `is None` guard stays outside both.
decisions.why: The existing hoist was right about ordering (a missing list must not orphan an ICmAnthroItem) but wrong about coverage: it left list_factory.Create() and the AnthroListOA assignment inside no unit of work at all, which undoable=True rejects outright. Generalises to any future 'resolve before the transaction' hoist - before must mean in an earlier transaction, never in none.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the hoisted mutations unbracketed (illegal under undoable=True), or folding them into the per-item bracket (reintroduces the orphan the hoist exists to prevent)

decisions.decision: For try/except cast sites shaped `try: x = ICast(arg); coll.Add(x) except ...: raise FP_ParameterError`, keep the cast inside the try but move ONLY the mutation into the bracket
decisions.why: Preserves the existing FP_ParameterError mapping exactly while still ensuring an invalid argument raises before any transaction opens. Applied to Person AddPosition/AddResidence/AddLanguage and Anthropology AddText/AddResearcher plus their Remove pairs in batch 9
decisions.rejected: Hoisting the cast out of the try entirely, which would let cast failures propagate as raw AttributeError/InvalidCastException and change the documented exception contract

decisions.decision: Bracket per branch inside each guard for polymorphic Delete dispatch (MorphRuleOperations.Delete's three ClassName branches)
decisions.why: An unmatched ClassName or a missing container must not open an empty named undo entry that Phase 2 would Rollback(0); per-branch labels also keep FLEx undo-menu fidelity (P4)
decisions.rejected: One bracket around the whole if/elif chain, which opens a transaction even when no branch matches

decisions.decision: Keep the dispatch guard INSIDE the bracket where every branch mutates (PhonemeOperations.SetBasicIPASymbol MultiString-vs-scalar, _path_b_attach owner shape)
decisions.why: There is no no-op path to protect, so hoisting the guard buys nothing and would split one logical write into two sites
decisions.rejected: Mechanically applying guards-outside everywhere regardless of whether a no-op path exists

decisions.decision: Treat __WireContext's multi-element path as a single unit of work rather than bracketing each mutation
decisions.why: If IPhSequenceContextFactory is unavailable after members are already added to PhPhonData.ContextsOS, those additions must roll back with it rather than leak into the project-wide owner pool
decisions.rejected: Per-mutation brackets, which would commit the member additions before the sequence create is attempted

decisions.decision: Install pyflexicon editable against the working checkout
decisions.why: FlexToolsMCP loaded flexicon from a copied site-packages install still carrying pre-B1 transaction.py (4 _transaction_depth hits, 0 UndoableUnitOfWorkHelper), so any verification routed through flextools_run_module would have exercised released code, not this branch
decisions.rejected: Leaving the copied install and relying on cwd ordering, which only happens to work for pytest run from the repo root

decisions.decision: Bracket the deep-copy helpers (LexSenseOperations._deep_copy_sense_to, __copy_sense_content) as ONE unit of work each, not per-field
decisions.why: A failure partway through must not leave the duplicate holding half the source content, or a created sense already in SensesOS with nothing in it. Extends decision 8 (multi-element wiring paths are one unit) from Grammar __WireContext to the Lexicon deep-copy chain
decisions.rejected: Per-field brackets, which would commit each copied property independently and leave a half-populated duplicate behind on failure

decisions.decision: Keep a filesystem side-effect OUTSIDE the bracket: LexSenseOperations.RemovePicture brackets only the PicturesOS.Remove, leaving the optional os.remove of the physical file outside it
decisions.why: The LCM cannot roll back a filesystem unlink. Enclosing it in a named unit of work would imply a reversibility that does not exist, and under Phase 2 a Rollback would restore the LCM reference while the file stayed deleted
decisions.rejected: Wrapping the whole method including the file deletion, which would make the undo entry a lie

decisions.decision: With the ratchet baseline at 0, keep the three ratchet tests but replace the scanner sanity check: test_scanner_runs_and_finds_entries (len(scan()) > 0) becomes test_scanner_is_functional
decisions.why: The old assertion would now fail precisely BECAUSE the sweep succeeded. A zero-violation scan no longer proves the scanner works, so the replacement pins the two properties it no longer demonstrates on its own: the scanner walks a tree containing real source, and its detection logic still flags an unbracketed mutation while not flagging a bracketed one. The ratchet itself inverts from a countdown into a permanent guard
decisions.rejected: Deleting the ratchet tests as the old docstring suggested, which would remove the very guard that keeps 0 at 0; or silencing the assertion, which the docstring explicitly forbade

Consequences: status-context.py falsely reports complete:true (resume dispatches nothing), and --materialize cannot flip any tasks.md checkbox, so they must be maintained by hand. Also status-context.py crashes on its own arrow glyph under Windows cp1252 unless PYTHONUTF8=1.

Live testing on Target surfaced FOUR pre-existing Notebook bugs that are NOT caused by B2 bracketing and were deliberately left unfixed to keep batch 9 mechanical. All are Category 8 (same-name fields with different LCM types) or wrong-receiver bugs, and all make the affected methods fail on any live project: (1) PersonOperations.SetGender/GetGender - ICmPerson.Gender is an int, not a multistring, so person.Gender.set_String(...) raises AttributeError; (2) SetEmail, SetPhone (writes PlaceOfBirth) and AddNote (writes Comment) target fields that come back as plain str, so set_String fails there too; (3) DataNotebookOperations.Create/Duplicate call repos.RecordsOC on an IRnResearchNbkRepository, but RecordsOC lives on IRnResearchNbk - needs IRnResearchNbk(project.lp.ResearchNotebookOA); (4) DataNotebookOperations.__GetRecordObject calls self.project.project.GetObject(hvo), but LcmCache has no GetObject, so EVERY record-resolving DataNotebook method is broken live. Consequence for this feature: the 16 DataNotebook sites bracketed in batch 9 are correct but currently unreachable at runtime, so their brackets could only be verified statically and by the scanner, not live.

The FlexTools MCP runner imports pyflexicon 4.3.0 from site-packages, not this checkout (flextools_start reports running_from_this_checkout: false). Any live verification of uncommitted work MUST purge flexicon.* from sys.modules, prepend the checkout to sys.path, and assert BaseOperations.__file__ before writing - otherwise it silently tests the released package. Note the resulting hybrid: the injected `project` object is still an installed-package FLExProject, which is why the legacy 'no LCM rollback API found' warning appears on stderr even though that string is absent from this checkout.

Live testing on Target surfaced THREE pre-existing Lexicon bugs that are NOT caused by B2 bracketing and were deliberately left unfixed to keep batch 11 mechanical (same call as batch 9). All fail BEFORE the bracket is entered, so those three sites brackets could only be verified statically and by the scanner: (1) ExampleOperations.SetLiteralTranslation/GetLiteralTranslation call self.__WSHandleAnalysis(), which does not exist on that class (only __WSHandle/__WSHandleVern) -- AttributeError on any live project, present at HEAD lines 1491/1520; (2) EtymologyOperations.SetSource/GetSource -- ILexEtymology has no Source attribute at all, CLAUDE.md Category 8 territory since Source is ITsString on ILexSense; (3) EtymologyOperations.SetLanguage is the worst because it does NOT raise -- ILexEtymology has no LanguageRA, but pythonnet accepts the assignment as a plain Python attribute on the wrapper, so hasattr flips False->True on that handle while a freshly-fetched LCM handle for the same Hvo still has no such field. Silent data loss. All three are xfail(strict=True) in tests/operations/test_lexicon_brackets_live.py; #3 asserts the CORRECT behaviour so it XPASSes the moment the bug is fixed.

The B2g ratchet has changed character now that the baseline is 0: it is no longer a shrinking countdown but a permanent zero-tolerance guard. Anyone adding a new LCM mutator anywhere under flexicon/code/ will now fail test_no_new_unbracketed_mutations, which is the intended steady state -- these tests are not scaffolding to remove once the feature closes. The module docstring and the replaced scanner sanity check both say so explicitly.
